Based on the web search results, here's a comprehensive overview of CUDA programming model core concepts:

## Thread Hierarchy

Threads are organized into a hierarchy to map to hardware: warps are the innermost level consisting of typically 32 consecutive threads executing the same instruction simultaneously, consecutive warps are grouped into blocks where all threads in a block execute on the same SM, and blocks are further grouped into a grid and are automatically scheduled by the hardware.

Each group of 32 consecutive threads is called a warp, which is the primary unit of execution in an SM. CUDA warps map to physical warps, so threads of a warp execute the same instructions at the same time (SIMD parallelism).

A thread block is a set of concurrently executing threads that reside on the same SM, share the resources of that SM, and cooperate among themselves using different hardware mechanisms. A thread block can be one, two, or three dimensional.

A grid is an array of thread blocks launched by a kernel that read inputs from global memory and write results to global memory, and can be one, two, or three dimensional.

## Hardware Mapping

A GPU has hundreds of Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), each containing numerous cores. Once a thread block is allocated to an SM, it will be further divided into a set of warps for execution. Every CUDA block runs on a single SM and cannot be split to run on multiple SMs.

## Memory Hierarchy

The highest level of the memory hierarchy is thread-local registers, threads in the same block share high-speed on-chip shared memory (SMEM) of limited capacity useful for inter-warp intra-block communication, and registers and SMEM are both SM on-chip resources while the off-chip VRAM called global memory (GMEM) is shared by all SMs and blocks.

Global memory provides much lower bandwidth than shared memory but orders of magnitude larger capacity, and the on-chip L2 cache helps speed up global memory access.

昇腾 AI 处理器的每个 AI Core 包含立方体计算单元（Cube Unit）用于执行矩阵乘加（GEMM）操作、向量计算单元（Vector Unit）用于处理逐元素运算、以及标量计算单元（Scalar Unit）用于处理控制流和地址计算。

## 存储层级架构

昇腾 NPU 采用 Global Memory (GM) → Unified Buffer (UB) → Scalar Register 的三级存储，其中 GM 是片外 DDR（GB 级），UB 是片上 SRAM（KB~MB 级）。

## 核函数（Kernel Function）

核函数（Kernel Function）是Ascend C算子设备侧实现的入口。在核函数中，需要为在一个核上执行的代码规定要进行的数据访问和计算操作，当核函数被调用时，多个核都执行相同的核函数代码，具有相同的参数，并行执行。

## SPMD编程模型

Ascend C算子编程是SPMD（Single-Program Multiple-Data）编程，具体到Ascend C编程模型中的应用，是将需要处理的数据拆分并同时在多个计算核心（类比于上文介绍中的多个进程）上运行，从而获取更高的性能。多个AI Core共享相同的指令代码，每个核上的运行实例唯一的区别是block_idx不同，每个核通过不同的block_idx来识别自己的身份。

## 存储模型（GM、UB、Local Tensor、Global Tensor）

存储单元即为AI Core的内部存储，统称为Local Memory，与此相对应，AI Core的外部存储称之为Global Memory。我们将用于存放AI Core中Local Memory（内部存储）的数据成为Local Tensor，将用于存放AI Core中Global Memory（内部存储）的数据成为Global Tensor。

Ascend C 的核心思想就是：将计算密集型任务分解为小块（tile），加载到 UB 中，在 AI Core 上完成计算，再写回 GM。

## 数据处理流程

数据需要先从Global Memory搬运至Local Memory，再使用计算接口完成计算，最后从Local Memory搬出至Global Memory。

Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about CUDA C++ programming concepts:

## SIMT Architecture

SIMT (Single Instruction Multiple Threads) is the architecture used by CUDA. A warp executes the kernel code in SIMT paradigm where all threads in the warp execute the same kernel code, but each thread may follow different branches through the code.

## Thread Hierarchy

A 3-level system is used: first we have the threads, then the thread blocks and finally the grid. A kernel grid is a collection of thread blocks, and a thread block is a collection of threads and represents an indivisible unit allocatable by a multiprocessor.

## Warps and 32 Threads

A warp is a set of 32 threads within a thread block. Within a thread block, threads are organized into groups of 32 threads called warps. All threads in the warp execute the same instruction simultaneously.

## Streaming Multiprocessor (SM)

Each GPU contains multiple Streaming Multiprocessors (SM) that are designed to execute hundreds of threads concurrently. Several thread blocks are assigned to a Streaming Multiprocessor (SM), and the threads of a thread block execute concurrently on one SM, and multiple thread blocks can execute concurrently on one SM.

## Best Practices

Thread blocks are best specified to have a total number of threads which is a multiple of 32, and when the total is not a multiple of 32, the last warp of the thread block will have some unused lanes throughout execution, which will likely lead to suboptimal functional units utilization.

## CUDA Compute and Memory Hierarchy Overview

**Thread Hierarchy:**

The thread is the smallest processing unit, where each thread runs an instance of a GPU program called a kernel. A warp consists of 32 CUDA threads that run in lockstep. A block (or Cooperative Thread Array) is a group of threads that cooperate together to process a slice of data and map onto the same Streaming Multiprocessor (SM). The grid is the collection of all blocks that run on all the SMs in a single device.

**Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs):**

The compute hierarchy within the CUDA programming model leverages multiple compute "perspectives" that get mapped onto physical streaming multiprocessor cores (SMs) on the GPU. The SMs feature a Single Instruction Multiple Thread (SIMT) programming model to achieve multithreaded data-parallel execution.

**Memory Hierarchy:**

The highest level of the memory hierarchy is thread-local registers, which CUDA provides warp primitives to exchange register data between threads within a warp. Threads in the same block share a high-speed on-chip shared memory of relatively limited capacity, useful for inter-warp but intra-block communication. Registers and shared memory are both SM on-chip resources, while the off-chip VRAM (global memory) is shared by all SMs and all blocks. Global memory provides much lower bandwidth than shared memory but has orders of magnitude larger capacity, and the on-chip L2 cache helps speed up global memory access.
